advances: Upper bound in actual volume-root units for the original ambient canonical circuit. The normalized support gaps are part of the data.

proof:
The nonnegative-domain tangent at $1/m$ has slope $c_d>0$, including $c_d=1$ for $d=1$. Thus
$$
E_d(h)\le\max\{d,m\kappa+c_d(h-1)\}
$$
for $h\ge0$, and for $h<0$ the left side is just $d$. Also $\eta\ge0$, with strict inequality for $d\ge2$ because $\kappa>r$. In the independent-endpoint bound, if $B\ge0$ the first weighted maximum is $a m\kappa+c_d B$. The second is $b m\kappa+\max\{-b\eta,-c_d B\}$. Subtracting the reference sum and dividing by two gives $(c_d B-b\eta)_+/2$. For $B\le0$ interchange endpoints and replace $B$ by $-B$. Multiplication by $V^{1/d}$ proves the bound in actual root units and gives its zero upper-bound range. The same rescaling of the attained central-range optimization gives its asserted intrinsic formula.

The endpoint sum identities give the first two intrinsic expressions. In an endpoint simplex the barycentric coordinate along the cap normal varies by one across the altitude. It equals $1/m$ at the centroid and $q_i$ on the original cut plane. Thus $s_i/h_i=1/m-q_i$ even when that plane misses the body, giving the signed-distance identities. On each threshold status the clipping formula gives
$$
q_i^A=1-(p_i^A)^{1/d}+(q_i^A-1)_+-(-q_i^A)_+.
$$
The last terms are the distances in altitude units to the vertex support plane on the empty-capture side and the opposite facet support plane on the empty-residual side, respectively. They vanish at tangency. Summing gives the asserted fraction-and-gap expression.

Under $x'=x-u z$, the new endpoint translation is $\delta+u$ and the new coefficient is $\beta_i+\ell_i(u)$. The effective shifts are unchanged and the coefficients sum to the same $B$, since $\sum_i\ell_i=0$. The scale of the reference simplex is also immaterial: replacing $T$ by $cT$ divides $a,b,\beta_i$ by $c$ and multiplies $V^{1/d}$ by $c$. Under an invertible continuous affine map all parallel plane separations for a given endpoint direction change by the same factor, and the signed altitude ratios are unchanged. The volume roots and $\widehat B$ therefore transform by the same volume-root factor.

statement:
For $d\ge1$, let $m=d+1$, $r=d/m$, $\kappa=(1-r^d)^{1/d}$, $\psi(q)=\min\{1,\max\{0,1-q\}\}$ and $\phi(q)=(1-\psi(q)^d)^{1/d}$.

Let $T\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional simplex of centroid zero and volume $V>0$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i=1/m+\ell_i$ for $1\le i\le m$. The convex hull of the lifts of $A=aT+\delta$ at $-1$ and $D=bT-\delta$ at $1$, with $a,b>0$, has actual midpoint fiber $K=((a+b)/2)T$. Take ambient halfspaces $H_i=\{(z,x):\ell_i(x)+\beta_i z\ge0\}$, with $B=\sum_i\beta_i$. Their endpoint barycentric cutoffs on the reference $T$ are
$$
q_i^A=1/m-\ell_i(\delta)/a+\beta_i/a,\qquad
q_i^D=1/m+\ell_i(\delta)/b-\beta_i/b.
$$
They satisfy
$$
\sum_iq_i^A=1+B/a,\qquad\sum_iq_i^D=1-B/b,\qquad
a q_i^A+b q_i^D=(a+b)/m.
$$
The endpoint capture fractions are $\psi(q)^d$. The actual volume roots of the residuals are $aV^{1/d}\phi(q_i^A)$ and $bV^{1/d}\phi(q_i^D)$. The closed residual is empty for $q<0$ and tangent for $q=0$, while the capture is tangent for $q=1$ and empty for $q>1$. For $0<q<1$ both have positive volume.

Define the normalized residual-root overshoots
$$
\Delta_i=\frac{a\phi(q_i^A)+b\phi(q_i^D)-\kappa(a+b)}2,
\qquad \widehat\Delta_i=V^{1/d}\Delta_i,
$$
where $\widehat\Delta_i$ is the actual overshoot in volume-root units.

Set $U=aV^{1/d}$, $W=bV^{1/d}$, $\widehat B=V^{1/d}B$, $\eta=m\kappa-d$ and $c_d=(r/\kappa)^{d-1}$. The global drift bound is
$$
\sum_i\widehat\Delta_i\le
\begin{cases}
(c_d\widehat B-\eta W)_+/2,&\widehat B\ge0,\\
(c_d(-\widehat B)-\eta U)_+/2,&\widehat B\le0.
\end{cases}
$$
Writing $h_i(A),h_i(D)$ for the corresponding simplex altitudes and $s_i(A),s_i(D)$ for signed distances from endpoint centroids to the original cap traces, positive on the captured side, one has
$$
\widehat B=U(\sum_iq_i^A-1)=-W(\sum_iq_i^D-1)
=-U\sum_i s_i(A)/h_i(A)=W\sum_i s_i(D)/h_i(D).
$$
For actual capture fractions $p_i^A=\psi(q_i^A)^d$,
$$
\widehat B=U\left[d-\sum_i(p_i^A)^{1/d}
+\sum_i(q_i^A-1)_+-\sum_i(-q_i^A)_+\right].
$$
The last two sums retain actual normalized support gaps. The effective shifts and $\widehat B$ are unchanged under a common fiber shear. Under an invertible continuous affine map, the ratios of signed distance to altitude remain invariant, and $\widehat B$ transforms by the volume-root factor. In particular the bound is nonpositive throughout $-\eta U/c_d\le\widehat B\le\eta W/c_d$. The sharp central range is $-\eta U\le\widehat B\le\eta W$, where the exact maximum of the sum of paired endpoint roots is $m[U\phi((1+\widehat B/U)/m)+W\phi((1-\widehat B/W)/m)]$.
title: Global intrinsic price for simplex circuit drift
